finding.claim: UNVERIFIED (PLAUSIBLE). scrub_css rejects url()/bad_url only when they are top-level children of a declaration. For non-shorthand properties, :ident children are kept using child[:value] with no url check. If Crass decodes CSS escapes in :value, an escaped open-paren (backslash-28) inside an ident becomes part of the ident, not a function token, so the url_flags check never fires. The decoded text is re-emitted and reparsed, yielding a live url(...) in the sanitized style attribute.
finding.source: style attribute on any allowed element, e.g. a p with style set to cursor, then url, then escaped-paren, then http, escaped-colon, then //attacker host path. Attacker controls HTML passed to Loofah sanitization.
finding.sink: Sanitized style attribute output via scrub_css and Crass::Parser.stringify, rendered by the browser. Causes external resource fetches (cursor or list-style url, tracking or IP disclosure), bypassing the library's url-blocking intent.

finding.guards_checked: url_flags check (line 104) covers top-level only. Shorthand keyword filter (line 127) does not apply to cursor or list-style. ALLOWED_CSS_FUNCTIONS (line 122) applies only to :function nodes, not idents. Reparse keeps only the first node, so semicolon injection is truncated, but the url() lives inside the first declaration and survives. Browser-side impact requires Crass decoding escapes in :value, which I could not confirm: the Crass gem is not installed locally and the WebFetch permission was declined. Run a quick Ruby check of Loofah.html5_fragment with that style attribute to settle it.
